_method: primary sources fetched live (gov.uk employer rates-and-thresholds pages for 2025-26 and 2026-27); verbatim quote in source.quote

entries.title: Employer NICs 15% above £5,000 Secondary Threshold (2025-26 and 2026-27)
entries.fact: Employer (secondary) Class 1 National Insurance is charged at 15% on earnings above a Secondary Threshold of £5,000 per year (£96 per week), in effect for the 2025-26 tax year and unchanged for 2026-27.

quantification.how: employer NICs bill for one full-time NLW employee: gross pay £12.71 × 37.5h × 52wk = £24,784.50; (£24,784.50 − £5,000 threshold) × 15% = £2,967.68 per year

source.quote: Secondary threshold: £96 per week, £417 per month, £5,000 per year ... [employer Class 1 contribution rate, category A] 15% ... Employment Allowance for 2026 to 2027 is £10,500.

entries.angle: At the 15% rate over a £5,000 threshold, a single full-time NLW employee now carries roughly £2,968 a year in employer National Insurance on top of wages — and because the threshold is low, every additional rostered part-timer above £96/week adds NICs, so overstaffed shifts across a multi-site estate compound at 15%.
entries.proof_pairing: Customer proof quantifying total labour cost (wages + on-costs) as a % of revenue, or hours saved through demand-matched scheduling.
entries.caveats: Rate and threshold verified as identical on the gov.uk 2025-26 and 2026-27 employer rates pages; the pre-April-2025 comparison figures were not fetched this session, so do not claim a specific 'up from' delta. Eligible employers can offset up to the £10,500 Employment Allowance (2026-27) against their total NICs bill, which materially reduces the net cost for smaller groups. Per-employee figure assumes a full-time 37.5h NLW wage; higher-paid staff carry proportionally more NICs. Category A standard rate; some categories (e.g. under-21s, apprentices under 25) attract different employer rates. UK-wide only; does not apply in Ireland (employer PRSI is a separate regime). This is a standing rate, not a fresh change — prefer it as supporting context or when the account signal is thin and no fresher entry matches.
